SAM OKAFOR
sam.okafor@example.com | github.com/samokafor | Vancouver, BC

SUMMARY
Final-year engineering student who enjoys turning a rough idea into
something that actually runs in production, end to end.

EXPERIENCE
Student Developer, Harborline Logistics (Co-op, Jan 2025 - Apr 2025)
- Built automated data pipelines with Python and cloud functions to move
  shipment records from partner systems into our internal warehouse every
  night, replacing a manual spreadsheet process.
- Put together a small web app where the browser-side screens (written
  with a popular component-based JS library) talk to a Python web service
  I wrote, so dispatchers could see pipeline status without emailing IT.
- Hooked that Python service up to a hosted large-language-model API so
  dispatchers could ask plain-English questions about a shipment and get
  an answer pulled from our own documents, with a link back to the
  original record so nobody had to take the answer on faith.
- Wrapped the whole thing in a lightweight container so it ran the same
  way on my laptop and on the company's cloud account, and kept every
  change in source control with a short write-up of what changed and why.
- Before shipping anything, I wrote a small test harness and ran it
  against a handful of tricky example inputs to make sure a change in one
  place didn't quietly break another.

PROJECTS
"Ask My Notes" (personal project, 2024)
- A weekend project that lets me search my own class notes in plain
  English instead of Ctrl+F. Splits the notes into chunks, turns each
  chunk into a vector, stores them, and finds the closest matches to a
  question before asking a hosted model to answer using only those
  matches.
- Added a self-check step: if the model's answer doesn't point back to one
  of the chunks it was given, the tool tries again instead of showing an
  unsupported answer.

SKILLS
Python, JavaScript (component-based UI library), cloud functions, hosted
language-model APIs, containerized deployment, source control, automated
testing

EDUCATION
B.Eng., expected April 2027
